news.title: Tinubu Rewards Flamingos Players With ₦100m Each After U-17 Women's World Cup Triumph
news.lede: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rewarded Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with generous financial incentives following their triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Each member of the victorious Flamingos squad will receive a ₦100 million savings certificate with Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank), while the team’s head coach has been awarded ₦100 million in cash. Members of the technical crew will also receive ₦50 million each in cash in recognition of their contributions to the team’s historic achievement. The rewards were announced today by Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who made the declaration on behalf of President Tinubu.

news.title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Team must win World Cup group to trigger rule. Spain, US, Germany and England currently in top four. The top four-ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa. Spain, the United States, Germany and England are currently ranked one to four in the world respectively, although the US and England still need to qualify for the tournament.

news.title: England: Harry Kane targets European Championships, World Cup and Champions League to add biggest team prizes to Ballon d'Or
news.lede: Harry Kane will become England's record appearance maker on Thursday night - but the Ballon d'Or winner now has his sights set on the biggest team trophies in football. England captain Kane will win his 126th cap for his country against Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley. The landmark moment comes just weeks after he was crowned the best player in the world. But while the striker has ended his long wait for team glory with back-to-back Bundesliga titles at Bayern Munich, as well as a German Cup, he is now eager to kick on again and land the most prestigious prizes for club and country.

news.title: Wenger considers run for FIFA president as Infantino faces backlash over World Cup rights sale
news.lede: Arsène Wenger (77), the former Arsenal manager, is considering a run for FIFA president. With controversy over current president Gianni Infantino's proposed sale of World Cup commercial rights erupting, European football circles are eyeing Wenger as a challenger. The British broadcaster BBC reported on the 10th (Korea time), "Arsène Wenger, the former Arsenal manager, is considering running for FIFA president against Gianni Infantino." According to the outlet, senior figures in European football have been hoping for weeks that Wenger would enter the race.

news.title: President Tinubu Rewards Flamingos with N100 Million Each for World Cup Victory
news.lede: The President also approved N100 million for the team's head coach, Akeem Busari, while each member of the technical crew will receive N50 million in recognition of their contributions to the country's historic achievement. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved a cash reward of N100 million for each player of Nigeria’s victorious Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, announced the rewards on Wednesday at a special presidential reception organised in honour of the world champions at the State House, Abuja, where she represented the President.She said the President directed that the N100 million reward for each player should be issued as a savings certificate to preserve the money for their future, given their young age.

news.title: President Tinubu Celebrates Flamingos’ World Cup Victory
news.lede: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has hailed the Flamingos’ historic victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup as a milestone for Nigeria and African football, describing the achievement as a defining moment for Nigeria and African football. The President gave the commendation on Wednesday during a special presidential reception held in honour of the young world champions at the State House, Abuja. Represented by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, the President directed that a ₦100 million reward be approved for each player and be issued in the form of savings certificates to safeguard their financial interests, considering their young age.
